design_rationale: Explicit random allocation of 4,418 eligible elderly hypertensive patients to strict- vs mild-treatment targets via a central registration office using a computer-generated list ("prospective, randomized, open-label study with blinded assessment of endpoints").

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was generated by a computer list at a central registration office after eligibility confirmation and consent (concealed from investigators until assignment), and the large baseline table shows no meaningful between-group differences.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Immediately after registration, the registration office randomly assigned the subject to either treatment group using a computer-generated list and informed the investigators of the treatment assignments."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was open-label so patients and treating physicians knew the assigned BP target and add-on drug classes differed between arms (inherent to a treat-to-target strategy), and ~18% in each arm discontinued treatment at investigators' discretion; however, an intention-to-treat analysis was used and dropout was balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The JATOS was a prospective, randomized, and open-label study with blinded assessment of endpoints... The effects of the two treatments were compared according to the intention to treat."

domain_judgments.rationale: Although treatment was discontinued in ~400 patients per arm, follow-up inquiries recovered outcome status for nearly all, leaving only 1.6% vs 1.7% without information, balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "responses were not obtained from 35 subjects (1.6%) in the strict-treatment group and 38 (1.7%) in the mild-treatment group (p = 0.71)"

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective cardiovascular/renal events adjudicated by an endpoint committee blinded to treatment assignment and to the BP time course, using identical criteria in both arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Endpoints were evaluated by the members of the Endpoint Evaluation Committee, who were blinded to the treatment assignments and the time course of BP."

domain_judgments.rationale: A pre-specified primary endpoint, protocol publication and trial registration exist, but the registration (UMIN000001021) was almost certainly retrospective (trial ran 2001–2004, UMIN number registered later) and the emphasized age-by-treatment interaction is an exploratory, multiplicity-prone subgroup analysis with a 75-year cut-point selected post hoc.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In the present study, we performed an exploratory data analysis to assess the contribution of various risk factors to the primary endpoint."

overall_summary: Randomization, outcome ascertainment (blinded adjudication of objective events) and completeness of follow-up were well handled, but the open-label treat-to-target design with substantial treatment discontinuation and the reliance on exploratory, post hoc age-subgroup analyses (with likely retrospective registration) raise some concerns. Overall risk is therefore "some concerns" for the primary endpoint and higher for the highlighted age-interaction finding.

paper_title: 3e84ac30_J of Clinical Hypertension - 2013 - Wei - Effects of Intensive Antihypertensive Treatment on Chinese Hypertensive Patients
design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint (PROBE) trial in which "A total of 724 hypertensive patients older than 70 years were randomly assigned to either intensive antihypertensive treatment or standard treatment by using a computer-generated table of random numbers."

domain_judgments.rationale: An adequate random sequence generation method is reported and baseline characteristics were well balanced across 17 variables, but allocation concealment (e.g., sealed envelopes, central/remote allocation) is never described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A total of 724 hypertensive patients older than 70 years were randomly assigned to either intensive antihypertensive treatment or standard treatment by using a computer-generated table of random numbers."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was open-label so patients and treating physicians knew the assigned BP target (inherent to a treat-to-target design), and the authors themselves invoke differential "variable daily compliance" between arms; an intention-to-treat analysis was stated, but no data on co-interventions, crossovers, or treatment discontinuation are provided.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "This was a prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint assessment (PROBE) study... That BP variability differed between the intensive treatment and the standard treatment might be attributed to a variable daily compliance with antihypertensive treatment."

domain_judgments.rationale: All 724 randomized patients appear in the analysis denominators and loss-to-follow-up was handled by censoring, but the actual number lost to follow-up per arm is never reported in the text (only referred to in a flow chart), so the extent and balance of missingness cannot be verified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Participants who were lost to follow-up or died of other causes were censored and were also included in the final analyses for the actual follow-up period."

domain_judgments.rationale: Endpoints were objective, hard cardiovascular events adjudicated with defined imaging/diagnostic criteria by an Endpoint Evaluation Committee blinded to treatment allocation and to the BP time course, applied identically in both arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In order to reduce investigation bias, endpoints were evaluated by the members of the Endpoint Evaluation Committee, who were blinded to the treatment assignments and the time course of BP."

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration number or pre-specified analysis plan is cited, the primary composite endpoint is reported alongside numerous unplanned component and subgroup breakdowns, and an additional secondary research question (visit-to-visit BP variability, analysed with a multivariable Cox model of unstated pre-specification) is reported with selectively highlighted significant predictors, creating substantial scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Cox regression analysis indicated that mean SBP (P=.020, 95% CI, 1.006–1.069) and standard deviation of SBP (P=.033, 95% CI, 1.006–1.151) were risk factors for the incidence of primary endpoint events"

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by Domain 5: the single-centre trial reports no registration or pre-specified protocol while presenting a large number of endpoint components, mortality breakdowns and an additional multivariable BP-variability analysis, giving considerable opportunity for selective reporting. Strengths include computer-generated randomization with well-balanced baseline characteristics and blinded adjudication of objective endpoints (PROBE design), although unreported allocation concealment, open-label treatment with acknowledged differential compliance, and unquantified loss to follow-up add further concerns.

design_rationale: Explicit central computerized 1:1 random allocation of 8511 patients to intensive vs. standard systolic BP targets, stratified by clinical center ("Randomization was performed with the use of a central computerized randomization program on a Web-based interface, with stratification according to clinical center").

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation used a central computerized web-based randomization program (ensuring concealment until assignment), and baseline characteristics including age, sex, BP, diabetes, and Framingham risk were closely balanced across the two large groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomization was performed with the use of a central computerized randomization program on a Web-based interface, with stratification according to clinical center." ... "Baseline characteristics were well balanced between the two trial groups"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was necessarily open-label (patients and investigators knew assignment, which is intrinsic to a treat-to-target design) and some patients discontinued the intervention, though a true intention-to-treat analysis was used and the achieved BP separation (126.7 vs 135.9 mm Hg) confirms the intended interventions were largely delivered; awareness of assignment could still influence co-interventions and reporting of subjective safety events.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Investigators and patients were aware of the trial-group assignments." ... "All analyses were based on the intention-to-treat approach"

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 2.7% of participants were lost to follow-up, balanced in magnitude relative to the event rates, with censoring at last visit and all randomized patients retained in the ITT analysis; mean imputation for missing covariate data is a minor concern given the small proportion missing.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A total of 234 patients (2.7%) were lost to follow-up before the end of the trial" ... "Patients who were lost to follow-up were included in the final analysis, with data censored at the time of the last follow-up visit."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome comprised objective, pre-defined cardiovascular events adjudicated by a committee blinded to group assignment, with standardized ascertainment criteria applied identically across groups; subjective safety outcomes (dizziness, hypotension) are more vulnerable to unblinded reporting but are not the primary outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Members of the adjudication committee were unaware of the trial-group assignments."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT03015311) with a published design paper, prespecified primary/secondary outcomes and subgroups, and an available statistical analysis plan; however, the trial was stopped early at an interim analysis for benefit (which can inflate effect estimates), no adjustment for multiplicity was made, and the prespecified app-management comparison is not reported here.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The data and safety monitoring committee recommended that the trial be stopped early on the basis of a clear cardiovascular benefit in the intensive-treatment group at two consecutive time points" ... "There was no prespecified plan to adjust for multiple comparisons."

overall_summary: This large, well-conducted multicenter RCT had robust central randomization, minimal attrition (2.7%), blinded outcome adjudication and ITT analysis, but it was unavoidably open-label (D2) and was terminated early for benefit at an interim analysis without multiplicity adjustment (D5), both of which may modestly overstate the treatment effect. The overall judgment of "some concerns" is driven by these two domains; no domain reached high risk.

design_rationale: The VALISH Study is explicitly described as a "multicenter, parallel-group, prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded end point" trial in which 3260 patients "were randomly assigned by the VALISH Data Center" to strict or moderate blood pressure target groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was performed centrally by the VALISH Data Center with stratification/minimization on sex, age, systolic BP, prior therapy and institution, which implies concealed allocation, and baseline characteristics were well balanced apart from a small difference in smoking prevalence consistent with chance across many comparisons.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "the patients were randomly assigned by the VALISH Data Center according to the following factors; sex, age (75 or 75 years), systolic BP (175 or 175 mm Hg), antihypertensive therapy, and institution (weighting coefficient: 2)"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was open-label so patients and treating physicians knew the assigned BP target and could adjust co-medications accordingly, and a large proportion of patients did not actually achieve their assigned target (only 1043/1545 and 733/1534 were within range at the last two visits, with achieved BP separation of only 5.4 mm Hg), although an appropriate intention-to-treat analysis was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All of the registered study patients assigned to treatment were analyzed on an intentionto-treat basis. In addition, a per-protocol analysis was performed."

domain_judgments.rationale: 181 of 3260 randomized patients (5.6%) were lost to follow-up and excluded from the analysed population, with no breakdown by group or sensitivity analysis of the potential impact of missingness, though the proportion is modest relative to the very low event rate.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Because 181 patients were lost to follow-up, 3079 were followed up until March 2008 or for 2.5 years"

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective cardiovascular events adjudicated blindly by an independent end point committee under the PROBE design, applied identically in both groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "End points and adverse events were blindly evaluated according to the prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded end point design by the endpoint committee and the safety committee, respectively."

domain_judgments.rationale: The design, primary/secondary end points, subgroups and statistical analysis plan were pre-specified and published in advance (rationale and design paper, 2004), and the reported primary composite end point, secondary end points and prespecified subgroups match that plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Statistical analysis was performed by Shin Nippon Biomedical Laboratories, Ltd according to the statistical analysis plan approved by the statistics committee"

overall_summary: Allocation was centrally randomized with balanced baseline groups, outcomes were objective and blindly adjudicated, and analyses followed a pre-specified plan; however, the open-label design with substantial failure to achieve the assigned BP targets (small 5.4-mm Hg separation) and 5.6% loss to follow-up without analysis of missingness raise some concerns. Overall risk is therefore "some concerns," compounded by the trial's acknowledged lack of statistical power.
